secondary_population: all 131072 fixed rows, including histories shorter than 2
supporting_endpoint: mean click BCE(off) - BCE(identity); positive means original correction improves over correction off in the same fixed model
all_labels: Report every label and equal-weight label macro, preserving negative effects

bootstrap.primary_weighting: row weighted: resample users, divide total sampled paired loss sums by total sampled rows
bootstrap.secondary_weighting: user balanced: average user-specific mean paired losses in each resample
bootstrap.scope: Conditional on this trained checkpoint, fixed evaluation window, and one fixed permutation of each type; does not quantify training, random-permutation, or population uncertainty

prediction_change: Per label and label macro: mean absolute, user-balanced mean absolute, median, p90, maximum, and fraction exactly changed relative to identity
gates: Complete receipt and hashes for raw predictions, metadata, plan, sources, and runtime gates
Exact row_index, part_id, row_offset, user_id, item_id and label agreement with immutable prior sample metadata
New metadata and predictions match exactly on all metadata columns
History-length eligibility recomputed from input; prior peer-based eligibility row IDs compared and any difference reported
Independent historical identity/full and off/local_off prediction comparison with declared tolerance
All probabilities finite within [0,1]; original binary labels retained
Identity-versus-plain, unchanged native Q/K/V across correction routes, and local native pooling permutation gates pass
Histories shorter than 2 have unchanged reverse/random predictions
interpretation: Sensitivity to correction-history order and on/off predictive utility are separate observations. This intervention does not show all RISE improvement arises from order modeling, does not replace retraining ablations, and does not establish semantic understanding.
